facts.fact: Formally described in July 2026 by Ralf Britz, Heok Hui Tan and Lukas Rüber.
Described in Raffles Bulletin of Zoology vol. 74, pages 606–623, as a new genus and species of miniature osphronemid.
Catalog of Fishes dates the description to 24 July 2026 and lists the species as valid.
It is the type species of the new genus Nanosphronemus.
The holotype is ZRC 70244, and 14 paratypes are catalogued as ZRC 70070.
The genus name combines Greek nanos ('dwarf') with Osphronemus, the family's type genus, and refers to the fish's tiny size.
The species name is Latin gemma ('jewel') and refers to the colouring of mature males.
It differs from all other anabantoid genera in its fin-ray counts, colour pattern and several unusual skeletal features.
Diagnostic counts include dorsal-fin rays XIX–XXI+2–3 and anal-fin rays XX–XXIV+4–5.
Molecular phylogenetics places the genus as the sister group of Trichopsis, the croaking gouramis.
Before its description, an aquarium importer considered it most closely related to Parosphromenus (licorice gouramis).
Before its description, it circulated in the trade as 'Microsphromenus sp. Vietnam' and 'M. sp. XD 11'.
Body length is 1.5–1.9 cm, which makes it one of the smallest known gouramis.
At rest, it has two dark longitudinal stripes on a light beige background.
During courtship, the upper dark stripe is replaced by a brick-red one and blue scales shimmer along the middle of the body.
During brood care, the belly turns bright blue.
Fish lose their colour when caught.
It is known from wetlands at an undisclosed locality near Huế, central Vietnam.
Catalog of Fishes records that it was collected from wetlands in an undisclosed area near Huế, central Vietnam.
Vietnamese nature enthusiasts first found it in September 2025.
The habitat was described as an open area at the foot of a mountain range.
The water measured at its home wetlands was very soft and acidic, around pH 5.5 and 22–26 °C.
It is a freshwater species.
It was in the aquarium trade before its formal description; the video presenter obtained his fish from a German wholesaler.
Few specimens are on the market, and the importer classes it as a fish for specialists.
A calm aquarium of about 30 litres or more is enough for a pair or a small group.
Recommended décor includes dense planting, floating plants, a layer of leaves and small hiding places such as coconut shells, clay tubes or roots.
Use very soft water, for example from reverse osmosis, lightly acidified with leaves, alder cones or peat extract.
Dim lighting is recommended.
Avoid sudden changes in water parameters.
Its aquarium care is most comparable to that of the tiny Parosphromenus ornaticauda.
It feeds mainly on small live foods.
It eats newly hatched brine shrimp, nauplii, cyclops, grindal worms, microworms and small daphnia.
Large bloodworm larvae are too big for it.
It often refuses dry food.
Several small meals a day work best.
Artemia nauplii are the main food in the aquarium.
It is a peaceful nano fish suited to a calm tank.
No reliable way to sex the fish is yet known.
In one keeper's group, females seemed slightly larger than males.
Presumed males show blue iridescent scales along the central band.
It builds bubble nests to breed.
Like its relatives, it is a cave breeder.
It has already been bred in aquaria; clutches are small, and one brood had 12 larvae.

care.quote: With a body length of 1.5 to 1.9 cm, which is less than an inch, it is one of the smallest gourami known.
Very soft acidic water with a pH level of around 5.5 and a temperature of 22 to 26 °C was measured there.
Very soft acidic water with a pH level of around 5.5
